title: Seller counterplay kit + pricing matrix (sketch)
content:
Goal:
- One-pager + deck skeleton SEs can clone during a live conversation when a prospect asks about price-performance tradeoffs or expresses reliability/regulatory concerns.
- Focus: quick technical counterplays, fallback economics, and a compact pricing matrix they can edit live.

Primary audience:
- Solution Engineers (field SEs), platform sellers, AE in technical deals.
- Secondary: sales engineers pairing with AMs on pilot scoping.

What this doc contains (working):
1) Ultra-short battle snippets (30s): single-sentence counter-answers to common objections.
2) Pricing matrix sketch by workload bucket + sample numbers for negotiation practice.
3) Technical counterplays (with one-liner justification + when to use).
4) Live-demo script: how to present fallback/rollout in 90s.
5) Quick checklist for pilot SLOs and what we need to commit (data, KMS, uptime).

Notes to self: rough, intentionally terse. Add slide deck frames after SE feedback.

1) 30s battle snippets (copyable)
- "We hear that latency matters — recommend Dedicated with a latency SLA and autoscale burst for peak windows; if you need <50ms p99 we can pin to smaller sequence lengths and use lower-quantized variants for throughput bursts."
- "If cost is the blocker, we can map typical throughput to a projected tokens-per-month number and show a tradeoff table: same prompt but 3 model variants with cost delta and latency impact."
- "For compliance: Private deployment with our KMS integration and audit logs — most customers onboard within 4–6 weeks when they provide a network IP allowlist."
- "Worried about hallucinations? We surface evals and regression alerts per rollout — can bind an eval prompt set to the canary so you get automatic quality rollback triggers."

2) Pricing matrix (sketch) — editable fields for demo (example numbers, not final):
- Workload buckets (rows): low-throughput exploratory, mid-throughput user-facing, high-throughput embedding search.
- Columns: Model tier (open-xxs / open-m / redwood-verified-large), Deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private), Estimated avg token cost (USD), Typical p99 latency (ms), Recommended batch size, Suggested discount/commit.
- Example row: mid-throughput -> open-m -> Hosted -> $0.0009/token -> 120ms p99 -> batch=8 -> pilot discount 20% on 3mo commit.
- Guidance: show 2 alternative cost points (latency-first vs cost-first) for the same workload so buyer can see tradeoffs on one screen.

3) Technical counterplays (when to use, one-liner justification, quick demo cue)
- Prefix caching + KV cache: "Use when most requests share the same prompt template (chatbots, assisted composition). Shows 2–5x token reduction for repeat-context flows." Demo cue: show a conversation where only continuation tokens billed.
- Model variant fallbacks: "Route to a cheaper-compatible model on non-critical traffic; reserve premium model for critical flows or hallucination-sensitive queries." Demo cue: simulated routing policy toggle.
- Quantization profile change: "Switch to int8/4-bit for high-throughput search; small quality diffs but 2–4x throughput improvement." Use when latency okay within a p95 window.
- Autoscale burst for Dedicated: "Protects latency spikes without long-term commit increases; show burst policy graph."
- Canary + eval binding: "Automated quality checks bound to a prompt set so rollouts can auto-failback on regressions." Demo cue: trigger a synthetic regression.

4) Live demo script (90s)
- 0–20s: Problem framing (customer pain: unpredictable per-token cost or tail latencies).
- 20–50s: Show pricing matrix, highlight two options (latency-optimized vs cost-optimized).
- 50–80s: Show routing policy: premium for critical routes, fallback for bulk requests; mention caching and quantization knobs.
- 80–90s: Close: propose a 30-day pilot: sample workload, 3-week tuning window, success metrics (p99 < X, cost per 1k requests <= Y, quality pass rate >= Z).

5) Pilot SLO checklist (what we ask the customer to commit)
- Representative traffic sample (1k–5k requests/day) or synthetic harness.
- Key evaluation prompts (10–50) for quality/regression monitoring.
- Contact: infra person for VPC/allowlist if private.
- Success metrics: latency p95/p99 targets, cost baseline, and quality gates (F1, accuracy, or human eval).

6) Objection roleplays (dialogue snippets)
- Prospect: "Your price is higher than other managed endpoints."
  SE: "Totally — let's map your actual request profile to three model paths and I'll show where our effective cost per useful-response is lower because of caching & batching; plus Dedicated gives predictability that avoids overprovision spend."
- Prospect: "We can't wait 3–4 weeks for private deployment."
  SE: "Start with Hosted + strict SLOs for the pilot to validate quality and routing; once validated we fast-track a private deployment with a 2-week ramp plan — we have a prepack checklist for regulated customers."

7) Quick rebuttals for technical objections (bullet list)
- "We don't control the model internals" -> "We surface model behavior with evals and run automated canaries; you can pin versions and revert instantly."
- "Latency is variable" -> "Use Dedicated pools, route by latency SLO, and configure autoscale/burst for peaks."
- "Embeddings cost too much" -> "Use hybrid approach: cached vectors for high-frequency queries + lower-dim embeddings for long tail."

8) Sales enablement artifacts to attach (placeholders to build)
- One-slide pricing generator (interactive spreadsheet) -> attach during call.
- 2-slide technical appendix: caching diagrams and routing policies.
- Pre-built demo repo link (internal) -> github.com/redwood-inference/field-demos/pilot-router

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Need real example numbers from finance for mid-throughput and high-throughput rows (ask finance for typical $/GPU and pass-through ratios).
- Validate claim: "2–4x throughput improvements from quantization" with bench results from serving-runtime team (ticket SRT-298).
- Add template for legal NDA + SOC compliance checklist for private pilot.
